s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with localized tenderness and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
Positive McBurney’s sign and rebound tenderness
key_facts: No history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness
Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with localized tenderness and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
Positive McBurney’s sign and rebound tenderness
key_facts: No history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness
Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium with a positive McBurney’s sign

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain and signs of peritoneal irritation

shortlist.label: Mesenteric lymphadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mesenteric congestion with prominent vessels and elevated white-cell count

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain and signs of peritoneal irritation

shortlist.label: Small bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and clustered small-bowel loops

shortlist.label: Malrotation of the intestine
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and abnormal location of the duodenum

shortlist.label: Volvolus of the small intestine
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal location of the duodenum and clustered small-bowel loops

shortlist.label: Intestinal ischemia
shortlist.why_kept: Mesenteric congestion with prominent vessels, although no signs of ischemia were seen

raw.rationale: The abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and the abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure are indicative of intestinal malrotation, which can cause acute abdominal pain and nausea.

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: The appendix appeared normal on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Intussusception
rejected.why: There is no mention of a telescoping intestine or target sign on imaging.

rejected.label: Mesenteric lymphadenitis
rejected.why: While the patient has abdominal pain and a high white-cell count, the imaging findings do not specifically support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of a Meckel's diverticulum on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Small bowel obstruction
rejected.why: The patient has normal bowel sounds and no abdominal distention, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Volvolus of the small intestine
rejected.why: While the patient has malrotation, there is no specific evidence of volvulus on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Intestinal ischemia
rejected.why: The CT scan shows mesenteric congestion but no signs of ischemia.

rejected.label: Intussusception
rejected.why: The CT scan does not show a typical target sign or telescoping intestine.
